requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap in the supplied tests for `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`. I did not request implementation source or run any searches.

**Mapping of obligations to tests**

- **SHA-256 over word-encoded structure, with the digest shape checked.**
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` in `tests/outline_content.rs` asserts that the Rust fingerprint value is 64 hex characters.
  - It also shows that `two words` and `twowords` hash differently.
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` and `string_literals_hash_as_words` in `src/outline/tests.rs` check the same word-separation rule, using doc prose and string literals.
  - The test does not compare against a known SHA-256 vector. The digest algorithm and the encoding rules belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, so I did not reassess them here.
- **The fingerprint scheme identifies the rules and their version.**
  - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts `languages::Rust.fingerprint_scheme() == "rust-structural-v1"`.
  - It also asserts that `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` retains the language's scheme.
- **Doc comments participate; ordinary comments are excluded.**
  - `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` shows that:
    - an ordinary `//` comment with different text, moved lines or changed layout leaves the hash unchanged;
    - editing `Doc.` to `Docs.` changes the hash.
  - The Rust case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` shows that `/* note */` and `/* edited */` inside a body leave the hash unchanged.
- **Inner and outer groups, delimiters excluded, consecutive comments hashed as one word sequence.**
  - `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` covers these `///`, blank-`///` and `/** */` cases:
    - `/// a` plus `/// b` equals `/// a b`;
    - extra whitespace and an empty `///` line do not matter;
    - `/** a\n * b\n */` equals the `///` form, so the `/**`, `*` and `*/` delimiters are not hashed.
    - Changed words and reordered words both change the hash.
  - `reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` covers inner `//!` comments and `/*! */`. It also checks the equivalence of `/** */` and `///`.
  - `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` covers word edits and reflow.
  - `inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups` shows that moving a word between the inner and outer groups changes the module hash, while splitting words across comments within one group does not.
- **Attributes attached to an item participate in its hash.** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` replaces `#[inline]` with `#[cold]` and asserts the hash changes. `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` checks that the `#[inline]` attribute is part of the selected item text. It also checks that reformatting keeps the fingerprint and that changing the body changes it.

**Marking.** All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

**Conclusion.** Each stated obligation has a positive test and a negative test, and the assertions enforce the expected outcomes. Nothing is untested.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
